title: Prospective Crossover Study Evaluating Patient Perception and Practical Performance Parameters of Guided Vibration-Controlled Transient Elastography (Guided VCTE) Compared with Conventional VCTE and Multiparametric Ultrasound (MPUS Including Shear-Wave Elastography [SWE] and Attenuation Imaging [ATI]) in Patients with MASLD
summary:
In patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), liver scarring (fibrosis) can develop over time. Today, various non-invasive diagnostic methods are used to assess the degree of fibrosis without requiring any invasive intervention in the body.

As part of their routine medical care, a non-invasive liver stiffness measurement is scheduled for these patients. Within the framework of this scientific study, different established and CE-certified ultrasound modalities for liver stiffness measurement are being compared. The aim is to better understand how these examinations can be integrated into routine clinical practice and how they are experienced by patients.
conditions: Fatty (change of) liver, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: FibroScan® model without Guided VCTE (conventional VCTE)
multiparametric ultrasound (MPUS, including SWE and ATI)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age ≥ 18 years
• Diagnosis of MASLD
• Indication for non-invasive fibrosis assessment by VCTE
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute liver disease (e.g., acute hepatitis)
- Decompensated liver cirrhosis or ascites
- Acute clinically relevant biliary obstruction
- Acute or decompensated heart failure
- Marked anatomical alteration of the right hepatic lobe (e.g., right hemihepatectomy)
- Bariatric surgery within the past 6 months
- Pregnancy
- Inability to undergo the examination or complete the questionnaire (e.g., due to a language barrier)
